title: The Akathist Hymn to the Most Holy Mother of God

stanzas.label: Kontakion 1
groups: To thee the Champion Leader,
~Mother of God our Lord,
Do I, thy faithful City,
~Glad hymns of thanks accord
For victory, and redemption
~From famine, plague and sword.
But since thy might, O Maiden,
~Resistless is and free,
Do thou from every peril,
~Whatever it may be,
Deliver me thy bedesman,
~That I may chant for thee:

stanzas.label: Ikos 1
groups: Gabriël, an Angel chief,
~With goodly message laden,
Down from heav’n to earth was sent
~To hail the Mother-maiden.
While with fleshless voice he spake,
~And born on earth fore-told thee,
Lord, he stood and stood aghast,
~For why he did behold thee
Taking flesh in Mary’s womb;
~And, as thou wouldest make her
Very Mother of his God,
~Thus Gabriël bespake her:
Hail Mary! by the help of whom
Joy shall enlight this vale of gloom:
Hail Mary! for by thee the curse
Shall fail from off the universe.
Hail Mary! who, for once and all,
Restorest Adam’s shameful fall:
Hail Mary! Maid, that shall conceive
The Ransomer of tearful Eve.
Hail Mary! Altitude sublime,
Which human reason cannot climb:
Hail Mary! Depth, far deeper than
E’en Arch-angelick eye may scan.
Hail Mary! for thou art the throne
Of Christ our royal Solomon:
Hail Mary! Bearer of that King,
Himself who beareth every thing.
Hail Mary! Star, that shall display
The Sun of justice’ brighter ray:
Hail Mary! of whose generous womb
The Word of God doth flesh assume.
Hail Mary! for, by thee subdued,
The whole creation is renew’d:
Hail Mary! for the Holy One,
The world’s Creator, is thy Son.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 2
groups: Conscious of her chastity,
~The Holy Maiden duly
Answer made to Gabriël,
~‘Sir, though thou speakest truly,
Yet thy word, so thinketh me,
~Is hard to be believèd,
When thou say’st, apart from man,
~A Son shall be conceivèd!’

stanzas.label: Ikos 2
groups: To the Envoy spake the pure
~And Ever-Virgin, yearning
For to learn a mystery
~Beyond the range of learning:
‘Tell me how shall babe be born
~Of damozél unwedded?’
Then he answer’d, full of awe,
~As one that inly dreaded:
Hail Mary! Mystic, knowing well
God’s counsel thrice ineffable:
Hail Mary! steadfast to conceal
What trust would have thee not reveal.
Hail Mary! Overture unpriced
Of all the miracles of Christ:
Hail Mary! Chapter number one
Of all the doctrines of thy Son.
Hail Mary! Ladder, stair whereby
Our God descended from on high:
Hail Mary! Bridge, that doth convey
To heaven the vessels form’d of clay.
Hail Mary! Vaunt and theme of love,
Oft utter’d by the Hosts above:
Hail Mary! ‘Daunt’ and ‘deathly blow’,
Oft mutter’d by the Fiends below.
Hail Mary! Parent of the Light
Beyond the bound of mortal sight:
Hail Mary! who hast, up to now,
Declared to none the manner How.
Hail Mary! that dost over-span
The wisdom of the worldly man:
Hail Mary! that dost light impart
Unto the simple faithful heart.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 3
groups: Then did Power of God most high
~Anon right over-shade her,
To conceive in Virgin womb;
~By means whereof he made her
Fruitful as wheat-harvest field,
~Which health and wealth supplieth
To each willing reaper-man,
~And joy to him that crieth:

stanzas.label: Ikos 3
groups: When, with God enshrined within,
~Our Lady had proceeded
And had met Elizabeth,
~Whose matters well had speeded,
Quick Elizabeth’s unborn
~Man-child with rapture bounded,
And, at sound of Mary’s voice,
~The praise of Mary sounded:
Hail Mary! Branch of vine, whereout
There sprung the Amaranthine Sprout:
Hail Mary! Branch and virgin Shoot,
Possest of rare untainted Fruit.
Hail Mary! Land, whose fruitful acre
Gave man his philanthropick Maker:
Hail Mary! that dost gender, rife
With bliss, the Gardener of our life.
Hail Mary! Blest, and fertile field
Which doth abundant mercy yield:
Hail Mary! Rich, as banquet-board,
With reconciliation stored.
Hail Mary! for, Maid-Mother bright,
Thou grow’st the Arbour of delight:
Hail Mary! for thou dost a fair
Safe Harbour for the soul prepare.
Hail Mary! for thy pleas from hence
Rise welcome as the frankincense:
Hail Mary! since, for all mankind,
Thy bedes with God acceptance find.
Hail Mary! for by thee we ken
That God hath Good-will unto men:
Hail Mary! for by thee our race
Hath boldness at the throne of grace.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 4
groups: Toss’d by sea of thoughts within,
~Just Joseph much did doubt thee:
And was minded, though thou wert
~A maid, to dwell without thee,
Deeming thee an other’s wife:
~But, after comprehending
That ’twas by the Holy Ghost,
~He sung, with joy unending:

stanzas.label: Ikos 4
groups: When in flesh came hither Christ,
~And Angels sung to greet him,
Shepherds heard their merry strain,
~And ran anon to meet him,
As their Shepherd. There they spied
~The Lamb of God, and proffer’d
Praise to Christ on Mary’s lap,
~And homage to her offer’d:
Hail Mary! Mother, and as dam
Alike to Shepherd and to Lamb:
Hail Mary: for thou dost enfold
Mankind, as sheep upon the wold.
Hail Mary! for thou art a screen,
Defence against the foe unseen:
Hail Mary! for thou dost suffice
To ope the gates of Paradise.
Hail Mary! for with earth to-day
The heav’ns entune a merry lay:
Hail Mary! for to-day glad earth
Unites with heav’n in holy mirth.
Hail Mary! for thy praise is sung
Aloud by Apostolick tongue:
Hail Mary! Courage unsubdued
For all the Martyr-multitude.
Hail Mary! Corbel, that up-stay’th
The cornice of the Christen Faith:
Hail Mary! Token, bright and fine,
Of Charity and grace divine.
Hail Mary! Hell, though well equipt,
Is by thee of his armour stript:
Hail Mary! for ’tis with thine aid
That we in glory are array’d.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 5
groups: When the Mages eyed the Star,
~The which to God-ward pointed,
By his rays, as by a lamp,
~They sought the Lord’s Anointed.
Thus did they approach and reach
~The mighty King of Ages,
God the unapproachable:
~Then sung for joy the Sages:

stanzas.label: Ikos 5
groups: These Chaldeän sons beheld
~God handled by his Mother,
Him whose hands have fashion’d high
~And low folk, one with other.
Him they ’knowledged, Lord supreme,
~In servile robe if dressèd;
Swift they honour’d him with gifts,
~And call’d his Mother, ‘Blessèd’:
Hail Mary! Mother of the bright
Eve-star, that sets not day nor night:
Hail Mary! Dawn, precursor-ray
Of Christ, the living Star of Day.
Hail Mary! quick to quench the blaze
Of heresy and erring ways:
Hail Mary! in whose light we see
The mystery of the Trinity.
Hail Mary! able to depone
Th’ inhuman tyrant from his throne:
Hail Mary! for of thy pure strain
Was gend’red Christ, that Lord humane.
Hail Mary! Thanks to thee, we see
No barbarous idolatry:
Hail Mary! for by thee we shun
Grim Tartarus, where filth is done.
Hail Mary! who didst quench desire
Of worshipping created Fire:
Hail Mary! Maiden, for thou dost
Be-free the soul from flame of lust.
Hail Mary! Guide, whose influence
Doth teach the Faithful continence:
Hail Mary! who, without alloy,
Hast brought all generations joy.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 6
groups: Home again in Babylon,
~The Magi spread the tiding
Of the Gospel to the folk
~In all that land residing.
But, obedient to their dream,
~Their journey they did alter,
Shunning Herod, foolish king
~Unversed to sing the psalter:

stanzas.label: Ikos 6
groups: Lord, in Egypt-land thy light
~Dispersed the shades of error:
Truth in lieu of falsehood shone,
~For, at thy face, in terror,
Saviour, Egypt’s idols fell,
~Unskill’d to stand afore thee:
But thy ransomed people there
~Extoll’d the Maid that bore thee.
Hail Mary! Means, whereby we men,
Once fallen low, uprise agen:
Hail Mary! Means whereby, we know,
Full many a Fiend is laid below.
Hail Mary! who beneath thy feet
Defeatest Satan’s arch-deceit:
Hail Mary! thou that dost convict
False God and idol maledict.
Hail Mary! Red-Sea wave profound,
Wherein proud Pharao’s host is drown’d:
Hail Mary! Rock with water rife,
Refreshing thirsty souls with life.
Hail Mary! Pillar, fiery bright,
That leadeth folk in mirky night:
Hail Mary! Shelter, that could shroud
The race, yet broader than the cloud.
Hail Mary! Pyx, whereof is fed
The soul with Manna, heav’nly Bread:
Hail Mary! that dost mix and give
Supernal joy to all that live.
Hail Mary! who, upon my chart,
The very Land of Promise art:
Hail Mary! out of thee, I trow,
Sweet streams of milk and honey flow.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 7
groups: Ere he left this present life
~Which fawneth but deceiveth,
Thee, Babe Jesu, in his arms
~The agèd Symeon heaveth.
He confess’d thee perfect God,
~And sung, in pure amazement
At thy boundless wisdom, Lord,
~His latest chant of praisement:

stanzas.label: Ikos 7
groups: To Creation there was shown
~A new thing by our Maker,
When he raised a tender shoot
~From out an unsown acre:
In this miracle of grace
~That so we may descry her
Maid before and after birth,
~And singing magnify her:
Hail Mary! for in thee we see
The flower of immortality:
Hail Mary! for we reckon thee
The garland-wreath of Chastity.
Hail Mary! for thy life depaints
The Resurrection of the Saints:
Hail Mary! for thy deeds declare
The life of Angels, bright and fair.
Hail Mary! Plant with goodly Fruit
That well the Christen taste doth suit:
Hail Mary! Tree, with leaf array’d,
And many rest beneath thy shade.
Hail Mary! who dost bring to birth
A Guide for waifs and strays on earth:
Hail Mary! Mother, whose good Son
Shall free poor caitiffs, many one.
Hail Mary! in the time of need
Who with the righteous Judge shalt plead:
Hail Mary! for thou shalt prevail
For many that do fall and fail.
Hail Mary! Over-mantling stole
Emboldening the naked soul:
Hail Mary! who more tender art
Than earthly lover’s fondest heart.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 8
groups: Let this strange and wondrous birth
~From love of earth estrange us;
Pilgrims here turn we our hearts
~Above, where he would range us;
For for this the lofty God
~Became right lowly, lying
In a manger, fain to draw
~Aloft his people crying,

stanzas.label: Ikos 8
groups: Wholly was the Word below,
~The Infinite, but never
Him from God the Father’s side
~Might this abasement sever;
For, for all that he was Man,
~From heav’n he ne’er retreated,
Being born of Mary Maid,
~By Gabriël thus greeted:
Hail Mary! Land that doth embrace
Her God, uncircumscript by space:
Hail Mary! Gate, that we revere:
In mysteries thou hast no peer.
Hail Mary! Name, the cause of doubt
To unbeliever stiff and stout:
Hail Mary! Theme of holy pride
To all believers far and wide.
Hail Mary! Sacred Car of him
Who rideth on the Cherubim:
Hail Mary! Chamber, meet for him,
Who bideth mid the Seraphim.
Hail Mary! Mother of that Child
Who man to God hath reconciled:
Hail Mary! whom on earth alone
The Mother and the Maid we own.
Hail Mary! for thou dost achieve
The undoing of the fault of Eve:
Hail Mary! for, at all device,
Thy Seed doth open Paradise.
Hail Mary! for thou art the Key
To Christ and to his Kingdom free:
Hail Mary! for we look through thee
For bliss and aeviternity.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 9
groups: Angel-nature saw aghast,
~Good Lord, thine Incarnation.
Mighty work of grace divine,
~When men of every station
To the Unapproachable
~Were let approach, conversing
With their God in mortal flesh,
~And sung, his praise rehearsing:

stanzas.label: Ikos 9
groups: Orators of many a tone
~Stand, mute as fish, confounded
By thee, Mother of thy God;
~For when hath speech propounded
How thou skilled’st to remain
~Aye-maiden? But astounded
We believe this Mystery,
~And let thy praise be sounded:
Hail Mary! Shrine and casket stored
With all the wisdom of the Lord:
Hail Mary! Magazine and Mine
Fulfill’d of providence divine.
Hail Mary! for, outside thy school,
Philosopher becometh fool.
Hail Mary! from thy tribune high
Professor proud is giv’n the lie.
Hail Mary! swift to mock the cant
Of hypocritick disputant:
Hail Mary! speedy to disable
And wither poets’ tale and fable.
Hail Mary! thou dost solve the maze
Of Athens and her quibbling ways:
Hail Mary! for thou fill’st agen
The seine-nets of our fisher-men.
Hail Mary! drawing souls to ground
From ignorancy’s depth profound:
Hail Mary! in the Name of Christ,
Through thee shall many be baptized.
Hail Mary! Ark upon the sea,
Where, whoso will, in safety be:
Hail Mary! Port, where mortal-kind,
Life’s voyage o’er, Fair Haven find.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 10
groups: Willing to retrieve the world,
~He, who did beautify it,
God, of his free-will and choice,
~Good Shepherd-like, drew nigh it,
God and man, for mortal sake,
~His Deity revealing,
He is known as ‘God with us’,
~In flesh to flesh appealing:

stanzas.label: Ikos 10
groups: Mother-Maid, a Wall to maids
~And all that seek and sue thee,
God, of earth and heaven King,
~With virtue did endue thee,
When he chose thy virgin-womb,
~To be his holy dwelling;
Yea, he taught all Faithful folk
~To sing, thy praise forth-telling:
Hail Mary! thee we mortals call
Pillar of Virgins, one and all:
Hail Mary! Portal, bolted fast,
Where in and out our Saviour pass’d.
Hail Mary! Leader, in due season
Renewing minds with sense and reason:
Hail Mary! Ruler of the quire
With heavenly Virtue’s heat afire.
Hail Mary! for thy Seed afresh
Regenerated fallen flesh:
Hail Mary! for thy blessèd Kind
Doth call the madman back to mind.
Hail Mary! for by thee to nought
Th’ o’erthrówer of the soul is brought:
Hail Mary! for was born of thee
The Sower sowing chastity.
Hail Mary! in whose wemless womb
Thy Maker found him cloister-room:
Hail Mary! bringing Faithful folk
Beneath thy Master’s easy yoke.
Hail Mary! Nursing Mother-Queen
To other Virgins clear and clean:
Hail Mary! whose good care provides
Safe escort for these holy brides.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 11
groups: Faileth Hymn that would recount
~The tithe, Lord, of thy mercies;
Were the sands upon the shore
~Out-number’d by our verses,
Yet, O Holy King, e’en so
~We could in no-way show thee
Due return for half the bliss
~That we thy singers owe thee:

stanzas.label: Ikos 11
groups: Unto men in darkness set,
~Pure Virgin, we descry thee
Sheen as lamp, equipt with oil
~For light, but kindled by thee.
Dame, thou leadest by thy ray
~To one true Light Supernal,
All mankind, who by their lay
~Extol thy name maternal:
Hail Mary! Beam of nothing less
Than Christ the Sun of Righteousness:
Hail Mary! Gleam of yonder Light,
Which setteth never, day nor night.
Hail Mary! Lightning-flash, that can
Illume the darkest mood of man:
Hail Mary! e’en as thunder-blast
To smite the enemy aghast.
Hail Mary! Plenteous Source of Light
That shineth in baptismal rite:
Hail Mary! Springing well of waters,
Wherein bathe Adam’s sons and daughters.
Hail Mary! from whose Shoot we trace
The Font-stone, with new Birth by grace:
Hail Mary! from whose Fruit we win
Free shrift for after-deeds of sin.
Hail Mary! Laver, that doth scour
The conscience clear as noon-day hour:
Hail Mary! Mazer-goblet fine,
Whose grapes are joyaunce, drink divine.
Hail Mary! Perfume, sweetly spiced,
And redolent of Jesu Christ:
Hail Mary! Life of mystick feast
For Christen people, West and East.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 12
groups: Willing to bestow free grace,
~That Lord, to whom are holden
All mankind for grievous debts
~From days that now are olden,
He in person, of himself,
~’Mid graceless men sojourneth,
And, destroying debtors’ bonds,
~Thanks universal earneth:

stanzas.label: Ikos 12
groups: While we hymn thy Son, our Lord,
~We sing thee too, his Mother,
Thee the Temple, by whose gate
~Came God, and not an other.
He, that holdeth in his hand
~The world, from thee progressèd,
Hallowing, blessing, teaching all
~Mankind to call thee, Blessèd:
Hail Mary! Tent, o’er all preferr’d
By God, e’en God the heavenly Word:
Hail Mary! Saint by all confest
More saintly than the saintliest.
Hail Mary! Ark of beaten gold,
Of God the Holy Spirit’s mould:
Hail Mary! Treasure-coffer, rife
With never-failing gifts of life.
Hail Mary! Diadem unpriced
Of Princes leal to Jesu Christ:
Hail Mary! Boast and Crown augúst
Of Bishops faithful to their trust.
Hail Mary! Strong, unshaken Tower
Of Holy Church, hour after hour:
Hail Mary! City-wall intact;
The fortress of our realm unsack’d.
Hail Mary! for by aid of thee
We lift the song of Victory:
Hail Mary! with thy succour must
Our adversaries bite the dust.
Hail Mary! who dost gently tend
My fragile body till the end:
Hail Mary! who dost eke control,
In Christ, the welfare of my soul.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 13
groups: Glorious Mother of the Word,
~God Holiest of the Holy,
Take this gift bestow’d on thee
~By us thy bedesmen lowly:
Rescue us, both great and small,
~From worm that never dieth:
And from every ill preserve
~Both him and her that crieth:

modern.source: A new translation from the Greek, made for Sanctify. The Greek text is from Wikisource.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 1
stanzas.text: To you, our champion and leader, O Theotokos, I, your city, delivered from terrible things, dedicate songs of victory and thanksgiving. Since your power is invincible, set me free from every kind of danger, so that I may cry out to you:
stanzas.greek:
Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ στρατηγῷ τὰ νικητήρια,
ὡς λυτρωθεῖσα τῶν δεινῶν εὐχαριστήρια,
ἀναγράφω σοι ἡ πόλις σου, Θεοτόκε·
ἀλλ' ὡς ἔχουσα τὸ κράτος ἀπροσμάχητον,
ἐκ παντοίων με κινδύνων ἐλευθέρωσον,
ἵνα κράζω σοί· Χαῖρε Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Ikos 1
stanzas.text: The first of the angels was sent from heaven to say to the Theotokos: Rejoice! And seeing You, O Lord, take flesh at the sound of his bodiless voice, he stood rapt in wonder and cried out to her:
hails: Rejoice, you through whom joy will shine forth;
rejoice, you through whom the curse will cease.
Rejoice, recalling of fallen Adam;
rejoice, redemption of the tears of Eve.
Rejoice, height too steep for human thought to climb;
rejoice, depth too deep even for the eyes of angels.
Rejoice, for you are the throne of the King;
rejoice, for you carry Him who carries all things.
Rejoice, star that makes the Sun appear;
rejoice, womb of God made flesh.
Rejoice, you through whom creation is made new;
rejoice, you through whom the Creator becomes a child.
stanzas.greek:
Ἄγγελος πρωτοστάτης,
οὐρανόθεν ἐπέμφθη,
εἰπεῖν τῇ Θεοτόκῳ τὸ Χαῖρε·
καὶ σὺν τῇ ἀσωμάτῳ φωνῇ,
σωματούμενόν σε θεωρῶν, Κύριε,
ἐξίστατο καὶ ἵστατο,
κραυγάζων πρὸς Αὐτὴν τοιαῦτα·
Χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἡ χαρὰ ἐκλάμψει,
χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἡ ἀρὰ ἐκλείψει.
Χαῖρε, τοῦ πεσόντος Ἀδάμ ἡ ἀνάκλησις,
χαῖρε, τῶν δακρύων τῆς Εὔας ἡ λύτρωσις.
Χαῖρε, ὕψος δυσανάβατον ἀνθρωπίνοις λογισμοῖς,
χαῖρε, βάθος δυσθεώρητον καὶ ἀγγέλων ὀφθαλμοῖς.
Χαῖρε, ὅτι ὑπάρχεις Βασιλέως καθέδρα,
χαῖρε, ὅτι βαστάζεις τὸν βαστάζοντα πάντα.
Χαῖρε, ἀστὴρ ἐμφαίνων τὸν ἥλιον,
χαῖρε, γαστὴρ ἐνθέου σαρκώσεως.
Χαῖρε, δι' ἧς νεουργεῖται ἡ κτίσις,
χαῖρε, δι' ἧς βρεφουργεῖται ὁ Κτίστης.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 2
stanzas.text: Knowing herself to be pure, the holy one says boldly to Gabriel: Your strange words seem hard for my soul to accept. How can you speak of a child born of a conception without seed, crying:
stanzas.greek:
Βλέπουσα ἡ Ἁγία,
ἑαυτήν ἐν ἁγνείᾳ,
φησὶ τῷ Γαβριὴλ θαρσαλέως·
τὸ παράδοξόν σου τῆς φωνῆς,
δυσπαράδεκτόν μου τῇ ψυχῇ φαίνεται·
ἀσπόρου γὰρ συλλήψεως,
τὴν κύησιν πῶς λέγεις κράζων·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 2
stanzas.text: Seeking to understand what cannot be understood, the Virgin cried to the one sent to serve her: How can a son be born from a pure womb? Tell me. And he answered her in awe, crying out:
hails: Rejoice, initiate of a counsel beyond words;
rejoice, faith in what must be kept in silence.
Rejoice, prelude of the miracles of Christ;
rejoice, sum of all His teaching.
Rejoice, heavenly ladder by which God came down;
rejoice, bridge that carries those on earth to heaven.
Rejoice, wonder the angels never cease to tell;
rejoice, wound the demons never cease to mourn.
Rejoice, you who gave birth to the Light in a way beyond words;
rejoice, you who told no one how.
Rejoice, you who rise above the knowledge of the wise;
rejoice, you who fill the minds of the faithful with light.
stanzas.greek:
Γνῶσιν ἄγνωστον γνῶναι,
ἡ Παρθένος ζητοῦσα,
ἐβόησε πρὸς τὸν λειτουργοῦντα·
ἐκ λαγόνων ἁγνῶν,
Υἱὸν πῶς ἔσται τεχθῆναι δυνατόν;
λέξον μοι.
Πρὸς ἥν ἐκεῖνος ἔφησεν ἐν φόβῳ,
πλὴν κραυγάζων οὕτω·
Χαῖρε, βουλῆς ἀπορρήτου μύστις,
χαῖρε, σιγῆς δεομένων πίστις.
Χαῖρε, τῶν θαυμάτων Χριστοῦ τὸ προοίμιον,
χαῖρε, τῶν δογμάτων Αὐτοῦ τὸ κεφάλαιον.
Χαῖρε, κλῖμαξ ἐπουράνιε, δι' ἧς κατέβη ὁ Θεός,
χαῖρε, γέφυρα μετάγουσα ἀπὸ γῆς πρὸς οὐρανόν.
Χαῖρε, τὸ τῶν Ἀγγέλων πολυθρύλητον θαῦμα,
χαῖρε, τὸ τῶν δαιμόνων πολυθρήνητον τραῦμα.
Χαῖρε, τὸ Φῶς ἀρρήτως γεννήσασα,
χαῖρε, τὸ πῶς μηδένα διδάξασα.
Χαῖρε, σοφῶν ὑπερβαίνουσα γνῶσιν,
Χαῖρε, πιστῶν καταυγάζουσα φρένας.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη Ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 3
stanzas.text: Then the power of the Most High overshadowed the Maiden who knew not wedlock, that she might conceive; and He made her fruitful womb a sweet field for all who long to reap salvation, as they sing:
stanzas.greek:
Δύναμις τοῦ Ὑψίστου,
ἐπεσκίασε τότε,
πρὸς σύλληψιν τῇ Ἀπειρογάμῳ·
καὶ τὴν εὔκαρπον ταύτης νηδύν,
ὡς ἀγρὸν ὑπέδειξεν ἡδὺν ἅπασι,
τοῖς θέλουσι θερίζειν σωτηρίαν,
ἐν τῷ ψάλλειν οὕτως·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 3
stanzas.text: Carrying God within her womb, the Virgin hastened to Elizabeth. And at once the child in Elizabeth’s womb knew her greeting and rejoiced; leaping as if in song, he cried out to the Theotokos:
hails: Rejoice, branch of the unfading Vine;
rejoice, keeper of the spotless Fruit.
Rejoice, you who tend the One who tends us, the Lover of mankind;
rejoice, you who bring forth the Gardener of our life.
Rejoice, field that yields a harvest of mercies;
rejoice, table laden with abundant pardon.
Rejoice, for you make a meadow of delight to bloom;
rejoice, for you prepare a harbor for souls.
Rejoice, incense of intercession, pleasing to God;
rejoice, atonement for the whole world.
Rejoice, God’s good pleasure toward mortals;
rejoice, mortals’ boldness before God.
stanzas.greek:
Ἔχουσα θεοδόχον,
ἡ Παρθένος τὴν μήτραν,
ἀνέδραμε πρὸς τὴν Ἐλισάβετ.
Τὸ δὲ βρέφος ἐκείνης εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόν,
τὸν ταύτης ἀσπασμὸν ἔχαιρε,
καὶ ἅλμασιν ὡς ἄσμασιν,
ἐβόα πρὸς τὴν Θεοτόκον·
Χαῖρε, βλαστοῦ ἀμάραντου κλῆμα,
χαῖρε, καρποῦ ἀκήρατου κτῆμα.
Χαῖρε, γεωργὸν γεωργοῦσα φιλάνθρωπον,
χαῖρε, φυτουργὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἠμῶν φύουσα,
Χαῖρε, ἄρουρα βλαστάνουσα εὐφορίαν οἰκτιρμῶν,
χαῖρε, τράπεζα βαστάζουσα εὐθηνίαν ἱλασμῶν.
Χαῖρε, ὅτι λειμῶνα τῆς τρυφῆς ἀναθάλλεις,
χαῖρε, ὅτι λιμένα τῶν ψυχῶν ἑτοιμάζεις.
Χαῖρε, δεκτὸν πρεσβείας θυμίαμα,
χαῖρε, παντός τοῦ κόσμου ἐξίλασμα.
Χαῖρε, Θεοῦ πρὸς θνητοὺς εὐδοκία,
χαῖρε, θνητῶν πρὸς Θεὸν παρρησία.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 4
stanzas.text: With a storm of doubtful thoughts within him, the chaste Joseph was troubled, for he saw that you were unwed, and suspected a hidden union, O blameless one. But when he learned that your conception was of the Holy Spirit, he said:
stanzas.greek:
Ζάλην ἔνδοθεν ἔχων,
λογισμῶν ἀμφιβόλων,
ὁ σώφρων Ἰωσὴφ ἐταράχθη·
πρὸς τὴν ἄγαμόν σὲ θεωρῶν,
καὶ κλεψίγαμον ὑπονοῶν Ἄμεμπτε·
μαθὼν δέ σου τὴν σύλληψιν,
ἐκ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου,
ἔφη·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 4
stanzas.text: The shepherds heard the angels singing of Christ’s coming in the flesh; and running as to a shepherd, they saw Him as a spotless lamb, pastured in Mary’s womb, and singing her praise they said:
hails: Rejoice, mother of the Lamb and the Shepherd;
rejoice, fold of the flock of the Word.
Rejoice, defense against enemies unseen;
rejoice, key that opens the gates of Paradise.
Rejoice, for the things of heaven rejoice with the earth;
rejoice, for the things of earth join the dance of heaven.
Rejoice, never-silent voice of the apostles;
rejoice, unconquerable courage of the martyrs.
Rejoice, firm foundation of the faith;
rejoice, shining token of grace.
Rejoice, you through whom Hades was stripped bare;
rejoice, you through whom we are clothed in glory.
stanzas.greek:
Ἤκουσαν oἱ ποιμένες,
τῶν Ἀγγέλων ὑμνούντων,
τὴν ἔνσαρκον Χριστοῦ παρουσίαν·
καὶ δραμόντες ὡς πρὸς ποιμένα,
θεωροῦσι τοῦτον ὡς ἀμνὸν ἄμωμον,
ἐν γαστρὶ τῆς Μαρίας βοσκηθέντα,
ἥν ὑμνοῦντες εἶπον·
Χαῖρε, Ἀμνοῦ καὶ Ποιμένος Μῆτερ,
χαῖρε, αὐλὴ λογικῶν προβάτων.
Χαῖρε, ἀοράτων ἐχθρῶν ἀμυντήριον,
χαῖρε, Παραδείσου θυρῶν ἀνοικτήριον.
Χαῖρε, ὅτι τὰ οὐράνια συναγάλλεται τῇ γῇ,
χαῖρε, ὅτι τὰ ἐπίγεια συγχορεύει οὐρανοῖς.
Χαῖρε, τῶν Ἀποστόλων τὸ ἀσίγητον στόμα,
χαῖρε, τῶν Ἀθλοφόρων τὸ ἀνίκητον θάρσος.
Χαῖρε, στερρὸν τῆς πίστεως ἔρεισμα,
χαῖρε, λαμπρὸν τῆς Χάριτος γνώρισμα.
Χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἐγυμνώθη ὁ Ἅδης,
χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἐνεδύθημεν δόξαν.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 5
stanzas.text: Seeing the star that led to God, the Magi followed its brightness; holding it like a lamp, they sought by it the mighty King; and reaching the One whom none can reach, they rejoiced, crying to Him:
stanzas.greek:
Θεοδρόμον ἀστέρα,
θεωρήσαντες Μάγοι,
τῇ τούτου ἠκολούθησαν αἴγλῃ·
καὶ ὡς λύχνον κρατοῦντες αὐτόν,
δι' αὐτοῦ ἠρεύνων κραταιὸν Ἄνακτα,
καὶ φθάσαντες τὸν ἄφθαστον,
ἐχάρησαν αὐτῷ βοῶντες·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 5
stanzas.text: The sons of the Chaldeans saw in the arms of the Virgin the One whose hand fashioned mankind; and knowing Him to be the Master, though He had taken the form of a servant, they hastened to honor Him with gifts and to cry out to her who is blessed:
hails: Rejoice, mother of the Star that never sets;
rejoice, dawn of the mystic Day.
Rejoice, you who quenched the furnace of error;
rejoice, you who enlighten those who know the Trinity.
Rejoice, you who drove the inhuman tyrant from his throne;
rejoice, you who showed us Christ the Lord, the Lover of mankind.
Rejoice, you who free us from pagan worship;
rejoice, you who rescue us from the mire of our deeds.
Rejoice, you who ended the worship of fire;
rejoice, you who set us free from the flame of the passions.
Rejoice, guide of the faithful in purity;
rejoice, gladness of every generation.
stanzas.greek:
Ἴδον παῖδες Χαλδαίων,
ἐν χερσὶ τῆς Παρθένου,
τὸν πλάσαντα χειρὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους·
καὶ Δεσπότην νοοῦντες αὐτόν,
εἰ καὶ δούλου μορφὴν ἔλαβεν,
ἔσπευσαν τοῖς δώροις θεραπεῦσαι,
καὶ βοῆσαι τῇ Εὐλογημένῃ·
Χαῖρε, ἀστέρος ἀδύτου Μήτηρ,
χαῖρε, αὐγὴ μυστικῆς ἡμέρας.
Χαῖρε, τῆς ἀπάτης τὴν κάμινον σβέσασα,
χαῖρε, τῆς Τριάδος τοὺς μύστας φωτίζουσα.
Χαῖρε, τύραννον ἀπάνθρωπον ἐκβαλοῦσα τῆς ἀρχῆς,
χαῖρε, Κύριον φιλάνθρωπον ἐπιδείξασα Χριστόν.
Χαῖρε, ἡ τῆς βαρβάρου λυτρουμένη θρησκείας,
χαῖρε, ἢ τοῦ βορβόρου ρυομένη τῶν ἔργων.
Χαῖρε πυρὸς προσκύνησιν παύσασα,
χαῖρε, φλογὸς παθῶν ἀπαλλάττουσα.
Χαῖρε, πιστῶν ὁδηγὲ σωφροσύνης,
χαῖρε, πασῶν γενεῶν εὐφροσύνη.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 6
stanzas.text: Having become heralds bearing God, the Magi returned to Babylon; they fulfilled Your prophecy and preached You as the Christ to all, leaving Herod behind as a fool who did not know how to sing:
stanzas.greek:
Κήρυκες θεοφόροι,
γεγονότες οἱ Μάγοι,
ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Βαβυλῶνα,
ἐκτελέσαντές σου τὸν χρησμόν,
καὶ κηρύξαντές σε τὸν Χριστὸν ἅπασιν,
ἀφέντες τὸν Ἡρώδην ὡς ληρώδη,
μὴ εἰδότα ψάλλειν·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 6
stanzas.text: Shining in Egypt the light of truth, You drove away the darkness of falsehood; for its idols, O Savior, could not bear Your strength and fell; and those set free from them cried out to the Theotokos:
hails: Rejoice, raising up of mankind;
rejoice, downfall of the demons.
Rejoice, you who trampled down the error of deceit;
rejoice, you who exposed the fraud of the idols.
Rejoice, sea that drowned the Pharaoh of the mind;
rejoice, rock that gave the water of life to those who thirst.
Rejoice, pillar of fire guiding those in darkness;
rejoice, shelter of the world, wider than the cloud.
Rejoice, food that takes the place of the manna;
rejoice, servant of holy delight.
Rejoice, land of promise;
rejoice, you from whom flow milk and honey.
stanzas.greek:
Λάμψας ἐν τῇ Αἰγύπτῳ,
φωτισμὸν ἀληθείας ἐδίωξας,
τοῦ ψεύδους τὸ σκότος·
τὰ γὰρ εἴδωλα ταύτης Σωτήρ,
μὴ ἐνέγκαντά σου τὴν ἰσχὺν πέπτωκεν,
οἱ τούτων δὲ ρυσθέντες,
ἐβόων πρὸς τὴν Θεοτόκον·
Χαῖρε, ἀνόρθωσις τῶν ἀνθρώπων,
χαῖρε, κατάπτωσις τῶν δαιμόνων.
Χαῖρε, τὴν ἀπάτης τὴν πλάνην πατήσασα,
χαῖρε, τῶν εἰδώλων τὴν δόξαν ἐλεγξασα.
Χαῖρε, θάλασσα ποντίσασα Φαραὼ τὸν νοητόν,
χαῖρε, πέτρα ἡ ποτίσασα τοὺς διψῶντας τὴν ζωὴν.
Χαῖρε, πύρινε στῦλε ὁδηγῶν τοὺς ἐν σκότει,
χαῖρε, σκέπη τοῦ κόσμου πλατυτέρα νεφέλης.
Χαῖρε, τροφὴ τοῦ μάνα διάδοχε,
χαῖρε, τρυφῆς ἁγίας διάκονε.
Χαῖρε, ἡ γῆ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας,
χαῖρε, ἐξ ἧς ρέει μέλι καὶ γάλα.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 7
stanzas.text: When Simeon was about to depart from this present age of deceit, You were given to him as a child; but he knew You also as perfect God. Therefore he marveled at Your wisdom beyond words, crying:
stanzas.greek:
Μέλλοντος Συμεῶνος,
τοῦ παρόντος αἰῶνος,
μεθίστασθαι τοῦ ἀπατεῶνος,
ἐπεδόθης ὡς βρέφος αὐτῷ,
ἀλλ' ἐγνώσθης τούτω καὶ Θεὸς τέλειος·
διόπερ ἐξεπλάγη σου τὴν ἄρρητον σοφίαν,
κράζων·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 7
stanzas.text: The Creator showed us, His creatures, a new creation when He sprang from a womb without seed and kept it incorrupt as it was before, so that, seeing the wonder, we might praise her, crying:
hails: Rejoice, flower of incorruption;
rejoice, crown of purity.
Rejoice, you who shine with the image of the resurrection;
rejoice, you who show forth the life of the angels.
Rejoice, tree of glorious fruit that feeds the faithful;
rejoice, tree of shady leaves that shelters many.
Rejoice, you who carried in your womb a guide for those who wander;
rejoice, you who gave birth to a redeemer for captives.
Rejoice, plea before the righteous Judge;
rejoice, forgiveness for many who fall.
Rejoice, robe of confidence for those stripped bare;
rejoice, love that surpasses every desire.
stanzas.greek:
Νέαν ἔδειξε κτίσιν,
ἐμφανίσας ὁ Κτίστης,
ἡμῖν τοῖς ὑπ' αὐτοῦ γενομένοις·
ἐξ ἀσπόρου βλαστήσας γαστρός,
καὶ φυλάξας ταύτην,
ὥσπερ ἦν ἄφθορον,
ἵνα τὸ θαῦμα βλέποντες,
ὑμνήσωμεν αὐτὴν βοῶντες·
Χαῖρε, τὸ ἄνθος τῆς ἀφθαρσίας,
χαῖρε, τὸ στέφος τῆς ἐγκρατείας.
Χαῖρε, ἀναστάσεως τύπον ἐκλάμπουσα,
χαῖρε, τῶν Ἀγγέλων τὸν βίον ἐμφαίνουσα.
Χαῖρε, δένδρον ἀγλαόκαρπον, ἐξ οὗ τρέφονται πιστοί,
χαῖρε, ξύλον εὐσκιόφυλλον, ὑφ' οὗ σκέπονται πολλοί.
Χαῖρε, κυοφοροῦσα ὁδηγὸν πλανωμένοις,
χαῖρε, ἀπογεννῶσα λυτρωτὴν αἰχμαλώτοις.
Χαῖρε, Κριτοῦ δικαίου δυσώπησις,
χαῖρε, πολλῶν πταιόντων συγχώρησις.
Χαῖρε, στολὴ τῶν γυμνῶν παρρησίας,
χαῖρε, στοργὴ πάντα πόθον νικῶσα.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 8
stanzas.text: Seeing this strange birth, let us become strangers to the world and set our minds on heaven; for this is why the most high God appeared on earth as a lowly man: to draw to the heights those who cry to Him:
stanzas.greek:
Ξένον τόκον ἰδόντες,
ξενωθῶμεν τοῦ κόσμου, τὸν νοῦν εἰς οὐρανὸν μεταθέντες·
διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ ὁ ὑψηλὸς Θεός,
ἐπὶ γῆς ἐφάνη ταπεινὸς ἄνθρωπος·
βουλόμενος ἑλκύσαι πρὸς τὸ ὕψος,
τοὺς αὐτῷ βοώντας·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 8
stanzas.text: The Word who has no bounds was wholly present here below, yet never absent from the heights above; for this was God coming down, not moving from place to place, and a birth from a Virgin filled with God, who heard these words:
hails: Rejoice, dwelling of God whom nothing can contain;
rejoice, door of a sacred mystery.
Rejoice, news that unbelievers doubt;
rejoice, boast of the faithful beyond doubt.
Rejoice, all-holy chariot of Him who rides upon the Cherubim;
rejoice, most excellent home of Him who is throned above the Seraphim.
Rejoice, you who bring opposites together;
rejoice, you who join virginity and motherhood.
Rejoice, you through whom transgression was undone;
rejoice, you through whom Paradise was opened.
Rejoice, key of the kingdom of Christ;
rejoice, hope of eternal blessings.
stanzas.greek:
Ὅλως ἦν ἐν τοῖς κάτω,
καὶ τῶν ἄνω οὐδόλως ἀπῆν,
ὁ ἀπερίγραπτος Λόγος·
συγκατάβασις γὰρ θεϊκή,
οὐ μετάβασις τοπικὴ γέγονε,
καὶ τόκος ἐκ Παρθένου θεολήπτου,
ἀκουούσης ταῦτα·
Χαῖρε, Θεοῦ ἀχωρήτου χώρα,
χαῖρε, σεπτοῦ μυστηρίου θύρα.
Χαῖρε, τῶν ἀπίστων ἀμφίβολον ἄκουσμα,
χαῖρε, τῶν πιστῶν ἀναμφίβολον καύχημα.
Χαῖρε, ὄχημα πανάγιον τοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν Χερουβείμ,
χαῖρε, οἴκημα πανάριστον τοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν Σεραφείμ.
Χαῖρε, ἡ τἀναντία εἰς ταὐτὸ ἀγαγοῦσα,
χαῖρε, ἡ παρθενίαν καὶ λοχείαν ζευγνῦσα.
Χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἐλύθη παράβασις,
χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἠνοίχθη παράδεισος.
Χαῖρε, ἡ κλεὶς τῆς Χριστοῦ βασιλείας,
χαῖρε, ἐλπὶς ἀγαθῶν αἰωνίων.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 9
stanzas.text: All the angelic nature was amazed at the great work of Your Incarnation; for they saw the God whom none can approach become a man whom all could approach, living among us and hearing from all:
stanzas.greek:
Πᾶσα φύσις Ἀγγέλων,
κατεπλάγη τὸ μέγα,
τῆς σῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως ἔργον·
τὸν ἀπρόσιτον γὰρ ὡς Θεόν,
ἐθεώρει πᾶσι προσιτὸν ἄνθρωπον,
ἡμῖν μὲν συνδιάγοντα,
ἀκούοντα δὲ παρὰ πάντων οὕτως·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 9
stanzas.text: We see eloquent speakers struck as silent as fish before you, O Theotokos; for they cannot say how you remain a virgin and yet were able to give birth. But we, marveling at the mystery, cry out in faith:
hails: Rejoice, vessel of the wisdom of God;
rejoice, treasury of His providence.
Rejoice, you who show the philosophers to be unwise;
rejoice, you who leave the masters of argument without an argument.
Rejoice, for the clever debaters have been made fools;
rejoice, for the makers of myths have withered away.
Rejoice, you who tear apart the tangled webs of the Athenians;
rejoice, you who fill the nets of the fishermen.
Rejoice, you who draw us up from the depths of ignorance;
rejoice, you who enlighten many with knowledge.
Rejoice, ship for all who wish to be saved;
rejoice, harbor for those who sail the sea of life.
stanzas.greek:
Ρήτορας πολυφθόγγους,
ὡς ἰχθύας ἀφώνους,
ὁρῶμεν ἐπὶ σοὶ Θεοτόκε·
ἀποροῦσι γὰρ λέγειν,
τὸ πῶς καὶ Παρθένος μένεις,
καὶ τεκεῖν ἴσχυσας·
ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸ μυστήριον θαυμάζοντες,
πιστῶς βοῶμεν·
Χαῖρε, σοφίας Θεοῦ δοχεῖον,
χαῖρε, προνοίας αὐτοῦ ταμεῖον.
Χαῖρε, φιλοσόφους ἀσόφους δεικνύουσα,
χαῖρε, τεχνολόγους ἀλόγους ἐλέγχουσα.
Χαῖρε, ὅτὶ ἐμωράνθησαν οἱ δεινοὶ συζητηταί,
χαῖρε, ὅτι ἐμαράνθησαν οἱ τῶν μύθων ποιηταί.
Χαῖρε, τῶν Ἀθηναίων τὰς πλοκὰς διασπῶσα,
χαῖρε, τῶν ἁλιέων τὰς σαγήνας πληροῦσα.
Χαῖρε, βυθοῦ ἀγνοίας ἐξέλκουσα,
χαῖρε, πολλοὺς ἐν γνώσει φωτίζουσα.
Χαῖρε, ὁλκὰς τῶν θελόντων σωθῆναι,
χαῖρε, λιμὴν τῶν τοῦ βίου πλωτήρων.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 10
stanzas.text: Wishing to save the world, He who orders all things came to it of His own will; and though as God He is the Shepherd, for our sake He appeared as a man like us; for calling like to like, as God He hears:
stanzas.greek:
Σῶσαι θέλων τὸν κόσμον,
ὁ τῶν ὅλων κοσμήτωρ,
πρὸς τοῦτον αὐτεπάγγελτος ἦλθε·
καὶ ποιμὴν ὑπάρχων ὡς Θεός,
δι' ἡμᾶς ἐφάνη καθ' ἡμᾶς ἄνθρωπος·
ὁμοίῳ γὰρ τὸ ὅμοιον καλέσας,
ὡς Θεὸς ἀκούει·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 10
stanzas.text: You are a wall for virgins, O Virgin Theotokos, and for all who run to you for refuge; for the Maker of heaven and earth prepared you, O spotless one, dwelling in your womb and teaching all to cry out to you:
hails: Rejoice, pillar of virginity;
rejoice, gate of salvation.
Rejoice, beginning of our new creation in the Spirit;
rejoice, giver of the goodness of God.
Rejoice, for you gave new birth to those conceived in shame;
rejoice, for you brought understanding to those robbed of their minds.
Rejoice, you who bring to nothing the corrupter of minds;
rejoice, you who gave birth to the Sower of purity.
Rejoice, bridal chamber of a marriage without seed;
rejoice, you who unite the faithful to the Lord.
Rejoice, fair nurse of virgins;
rejoice, you who adorn holy souls as brides.
stanzas.greek:
Τεῖχος εἶ τῶν παρθένων,
Θεοτόκε Παρθένε,
καὶ πάντων τῶν εἰς σὲ προστρεχόντων.
Ὁ γὰρ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς,
κατεσκεύασέ σε ποιητής, Ἄχραντε,
οἰκήσας ἐν τῇ μήτρᾳ σου,
καὶ πάντας σοι προσφωνεῖν διδάξας·
Χαῖρε, ἡ στήλη τῆς παρθενίας,
χαῖρε, ἡ πύλη τῆς σωτήριας.
Χαῖρε, ἀρχηγὲ νοητῆς ἀναπλάσεως,
χαῖρε, χορηγὲ θεϊκῆς ἀγαθότητος.
Χαῖρε, σὺ γὰρ ἀνεγέννησας τοὺς συλληφθέντας αἰσχρῶς,
χαῖρε, σὺ γὰρ ἐνουθέτησας τοὺς συληθέντας τὸν νοῦν.
Χαῖρε, ἡ τὸν φθορέα τῶν φρενῶν καταργοῦσα,
χαῖρε, ἡ τὸν σπορέα τῆς ἁγνείας τεκοῦσα.
Χαῖρε, παστάς ἀσπόρου νυμφεύσεως,
χαῖρε, πιστοὺς Κυρίῳ ἁρμόζουσα.
Χαῖρε, καλὴ κουροτρόφε παρθένων,
χαῖρε, ψυχῶν νυμφοστόλε ἁγίων.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 11
stanzas.text: Every hymn falls short that strives to match the multitude of Your great mercies; for though we offer You songs as many as the grains of sand, O holy King, we do nothing worthy of what You have given to us who cry to You:
stanzas.greek:
Ὕμνος ἅπας ἡττᾶται,
συνεκτείνεσθαι σπεύδων,
τῷ πλήθει τῶν πολλῶν οἰκτιρμῶν σου·
ἰσαρίθμους γὰρ τῇ ψάμμῳ ὠδάς,
ἂν προσφέρωμέν σοι, Βασιλεῦ ἅγιε,
οὐδὲν τελοῦμεν ἄξιον,
ὧν δέδωκας ἡμῖν τοῖς σοὶ βοῶσιν·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 11
stanzas.text: We see the holy Virgin as a lamp that receives the light and shines on those in darkness; for kindling the light that is not of this world, she leads all to the knowledge of God, enlightening the mind with her radiance, and is honored with this cry:
hails: Rejoice, ray of the spiritual Sun;
rejoice, beam of the Light that never sets.
Rejoice, lightning that shines upon souls;
rejoice, for like thunder you strike down the enemies.
Rejoice, for you make the radiance of many lights to dawn;
rejoice, for you pour forth the river of many streams.
Rejoice, you who prefigure the font of baptism;
rejoice, you who wash away the stain of sin.
Rejoice, basin that washes the conscience clean;
rejoice, cup that mingles the wine of joy.
Rejoice, fragrance of the sweetness of Christ;
rejoice, life of the mystical feast.
stanzas.greek:
Φωτοδόχον λαμπάδα,
τοῖς ἐν σκότει φανεῖσαν,
ὁρῶμεν τὴν ἁγίαν Παρθένον·
τὸ γὰρ ἄυλον ἅπτουσα φῶς,
ὁδηγεῖ πρὸς γνῶσιν θεϊκὴν ἅπαντας,
αὐγῇ τὸν νοῦν φωτίζουσα,
κραυγῇ δὲ τιμωμένη ταῦτα·
Χαῖρε, ἀκτὶς νοητοῦ ἡλίου,
χαῖρε, βολὶς τοῦ ἀδύτου φέγγους.
Χαῖρε, ἀστραπὴ τὰς ψυχὰς καταλάμπουσα,
χαῖρε, ὡς βροντὴ τοὺς ἐχθροὺς καταπλήττουσα.
Χαῖρε, ὅτι τὸν πολύφωτον ἀνατέλλεις φωτισμόν,
Χαῖρε, ὅτι τὸν πολύρρυτον ἀναβλύζεις ποταμόν.
Χαῖρε, τῆς κολυμβήθρας ζωγραφοῦσα τὸν τύπον,
χαῖρε, τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἀναιροῦσα τὸν ρύπον.
Χαῖρε, λουτὴρ ἔκπλυνων συνείδησιν,
χαῖρε, κρατὴρ κιρνῶν ἀγαλλίασιν.
Χαῖρε, ὀσμὴ τῆς Χριστοῦ εὐωδίας,
χαῖρε, ζωὴ μυστικῆς εὐωχίας.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 12
stanzas.text: Wishing to grant forgiveness of ancient debts, He who pays the debts of all people came Himself to live among those who had wandered from His grace; and tearing up the record of our debt, He hears from all:
stanzas.greek:
Χάριν δοῦναι θελήσας,
ὀφλημάτων ἀρχαίων,
ὁ πάντων χρεωλύτης ἀνθρώπων,
ἐπεδήμησε δι’ ἑαυτοῦ,
πρὸς τοὺς ἀποδήμους τῆς αὐτοῦ Χάριτος·
καὶ σχίσας τὸ χειρόγραφον,
ἀκούει παρὰ πάντων οὕτως·
Ἀλληλούια.

stanzas.label: Ikos 12
stanzas.text: Singing of your Child, we all praise you as a living temple, O Theotokos; for the Lord who holds all things in His hand dwelt in your womb, and made you holy and glorious, and taught all to cry out to you:
hails: Rejoice, tabernacle of God the Word;
rejoice, holy one, greater than the Holy of Holies.
Rejoice, ark made golden by the Spirit;
rejoice, treasury of life that is never spent.
Rejoice, precious crown of devout rulers;
rejoice, honored boast of reverent priests.
Rejoice, unshaken tower of the Church;
rejoice, wall of the Kingdom that cannot be breached.
Rejoice, you through whom victories are won;
rejoice, you through whom enemies fall.
Rejoice, healing of my body;
rejoice, salvation of my soul.
stanzas.greek:
Ψάλλοντές σου τὸν τόκον,
ἀνυμνοῦμέν σε πάντες,
ὡς ἔμψυχον ναόν, Θεοτόκε.
Ἐν τῇ σῇ γὰρ οἰκήσας γαστρί,
ὁ συνέχων πάντα τῇ χειρὶ Κύριος,
ἡγίασεν, ἐδόξασεν, ἐδίδαξε βοᾶν σοὶ πάντας·
Χαῖρε, σκηνὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Λόγου,
χαῖρε, Ἁγία ἁγίων μείζων.
Χαῖρε, κιβωτὲ χρυσωθεῖσα τῷ Πνεύματι,
χαῖρε, θησαυρὲ τῆς ζωῆς ἀδαπάνητε.
Χαῖρε, τίμιον διάδημα βασιλέων εὐσεβῶν,
χαῖρε, καύχημα σεβάσμιον ἱερέων εὐλαβῶν.
Χαῖρε, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ὁ ἀσάλευτος πύργος,
χαῖρε, τῆς Βασιλείας τὸ ἀπόρθητον τεῖχος.
Χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἐγείρονται τρόπαια,
χαῖρε, δι' ἧς ἐχθροὶ καταπίπτουσι.
Χαῖρε, χρωτὸς τοῦ ἐμοῦ θεραπεία,
χαῖρε, ψυχῆς τῆς ἐμῆς σωτηρία.
Χαῖρε, Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

stanzas.label: Kontakion 13
stanzas.text: O Mother praised by all, who gave birth to the Word, the holiest of all the saints: accept this offering now, deliver all from every misfortune, and rescue from the punishment to come those who cry to you:
stanzas.greek:
Ὦ πανύμνητε Μῆτερ,
ἡ τεκοῦσα τὸν πάντων ἁγίων,
ἁγιώτατον Λόγον·
δεξαμένη γὰρ τὴν νῦν προσφοράν,
ἀπὸ πάσης ρῦσαι συμφορᾶς ἅπαντας,
καὶ τῆς μελλούσης λύτρωσαι κολάσεως,
τοὺς σοὶ βοῶντας·
Ἀλληλούια.

annunciation.label: Another kontakion
annunciation.text: The bodiless one, understanding the command given him in secret, came in haste to the house of Joseph and said to the Maiden who knew not wedlock: He who bowed the heavens and came down is wholly contained in you, yet unchanged. Seeing Him in your womb, taking the form of a servant, I stand in awe and cry to you:
annunciation.greek:
Τὸ προσταχθὲν μυστικῶς λαβὼν ἐν γνώσει,
ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ σπουδῇ ἐπέστη,
ὁ ἀσώματος λέγων τῇ Ἀπειρογάμῳ·
ὁ κλίνας ἐν καταβάσει τοὺς οὐρανούς,
χωρεῑται ἀναλλοιώτως ὅλος ἐν σοι·
Ὃν καὶ βλέπων ἐν μήτρᾳ σου,
λαβόντα δούλου μορφήν,
ἐξίσταμαι κραυγάζων σοι·
Χαῖρε Νύμφη ἀνύμφευτε.

woodward_source: Done into English verse by G. R. Woodward, edited with W. J. Birkbeck (Oxford, 1917). Public domain.
